correctness.rationale: Complete resetting selects a regenerative stationary law. The five generator moments close, since all five observables vanish at reset. Substitution gives 2F over a strictly positive denominator; at p=0 it reduces to r/(4β+r). For each positive r the leading activity coefficient A has exactly one positive simple zero by Descartes' rule and its opposite endpoint signs. The positive activity root P_r exists beyond this zero and diverges at both ends of its trap domain, so its minimum is attained. At fixed activity the leading, linear and constant trap coefficients of F are positive, and only its cubic and quadratic coefficients can be negative. Descartes' rule therefore bounds the positive trap roots, counted with multiplicity, by two. At the minimum activity any zero is a local minimum and has even multiplicity, proving uniqueness and exact multiplicity two. Above it the negative value at the minimizing trap and positive values at both ends force two simple roots. F_p<0 and F_ββ>0 at the fold give the stated square-root opening. For the weak limit, P_r²/r≥C/[r(−A)] gives uniform coercivity at zero and infinity; on compact positive trap intervals the rescaled root converges to √G, whose derivative has precisely one positive zero. For the strong limit the coefficient of z² is (2t+1)(1+t−3t²); the rescaled bound C/[r²(−A)] diverges for large t uniformly at large r and along any sequence approaching the moving coefficient-zero boundary. The limiting quartic has the same two-root bound, so its positive branch has a unique minimum. Local convergence and both compactness arguments justify the limiting minima. Independently checked rational test triples agree with the factorized identity. Replay the numerical constants by solving F=F_β=0 at r=1, the weak-limit quartic and the strong-limit Φ=Φ_t=0; the independently obtained values agree to the quoted precision, apart from rounding. At r=1 and p=100, the two roots are approximately 0.7689475143 and 4828.575391.
residual_risks: The frozen recurrence is the basis for correctness; the printed expanded equation (21) in Shee does not literally agree in its activity-independent linear trap term. At r=β=1 and p=0 the printed equation gives 257/1575, whereas the recurrence and Shee's stated passive special case both give 1/5. This is an apparent typo in the cited expansion, not a counterexample to the frozen theorem.
The threshold is p_c in p=Pe², or √p_c in Pe. A zero of the radial statistic does not imply a Gaussian stationary law.
The computations are numerical corroboration of constants and finite checks of the identity, not proofs of the continuum classification.

value.rationale: The exact phase geometry resolves an existing numerically identified phenomenon: it excludes hidden additional sign intervals at any positive reset rate, distinguishes the unique double-root threshold from simple crossings, and gives the opening and the scales required to reach it in two singular regimes. These furnish quantitative diagnostics for the radial fourth moment beyond recalculation of a known phase plot.
residual_risks: The phase is a sign of one stationary statistic, not a thermodynamic transition or a claim about arbitrary reset protocols.
